sentences.text: 3. Learned counsel for the appellant submits that learned Tribunal has not awarded sufficient amount for compensation.
It is submitted that doctor had assessed the permanent disability on face and hand at 50% and it was accepted by the Tribunal.

She was bedridden for six months due to the grievous injuries and merely on the ground that appellant has neither filed a copy of her application nor examined any employee of WCL has not accepted her unchallenged statement.
It is settled law that strict proof is not required in Motor Accident Claim cases.
Tribunal has also erred in not holding that she was compelled to take voluntary retirement.

It is further submitted that appellant was Welfare Inspector and she tried to perform her duties effectively and sincerely for one and a half years but when she failed to perform her work she had to seek voluntary retirement in 2000.
The age of superannuation was 60 years before attaining the age of superannuation losing monthly salary of Rs.8130/- for four years.
In view of the above submission, appeal be allowed and compensation be suitably enhanced.
4. Learned counsel for the respondent No.3 Insurance Company submits that the compensation awarded by Tribunal is just and proper and no enhancement is required.
5. I have heard the learned counsel for the parties and perused the record of the case.
6. In this case, claimant/appellant has not submitted any document to the extent that when she was bedridden she did not receive salary of six months from her concerned department.
Claimant has also not produced application of voluntary retirement which she has submitted in her department.
Appellant has neither produced any witness nor any statement was recorded to prove that she has taken voluntary retirement due to said accident.

Learned Tribunal in Para-15 of the impugned award has properly appreciated the oral and documentary evidence and recorded finding that claimant has not proved that due to the accident, she has taken voluntary retirement four years before attaining the age of superannuation.

7. From perusal of record, it is found that appellant was admitted to Padhar Hospital Betul from 21.05.1998 to 05.06.1998 and thereafter she was admitted to the Kunal Hospital from 10.09.1998 to 20.09.1998.
Appellant sustained grievous injuries and she was admitted to hospital for a long time.
As per permanent disability certificate, total 50% of disability is ascertained.

Therefore, it appears that total amount of Rs.1,23,000/- awarded by the Tribunal is found to be on lower side, however,
considering the nature and facts of the case, this Court deems it appropriate to enhance the compensation amount awarded by learned Claims Tribunal.
8.

In view of above discussion, Rs.14,000/- be enhanced for Special diet, Rs.18,000/- be enhanced for attender and nurse, Rs.10,000/- be enhanced for transportation, Rs.20,000/- be enhanced for mental and physical pain and Rs.50,000/- be given for permanent disability.

Therefore, the enhanced amount comes to Rs.1,12,000/-
9.

The enhanced amount of compensation i.e. Rs.1,12,000/-(Rupees One Lac Twelve Thousand only) shall carry interest as awarded by learned claims tribunal from the date of claim application Smt.Nalini Shrivastava vs K.V.Tapkale & Ors on 15 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/150560152/
2 till realization.
The enhanced amount of compensation shall be payable to the appellant - claimant by the Insurance Company within a period of 12 weeks from the date of production of certified copy of this order.
Rest of the award passed by learned claims tribunal shall remain intact.
10. Present miscellaneous appeal is disposed of in above terms.
Records of the learned Claims Tribunal be sent back.

(PRAMOD KUMAR AGRAWAL) JUDGE shahina Smt.Nalini Shrivastava vs K.V.Tapkale & Ors on 15 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/150560152/
